page: Google Cloud Platform c3-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine configuration featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores and 16 GB of system memory. Powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8481C processor running at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz, the instance provides 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware features include an allocation of 48 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and access to 105 MB of L3 cache. The processor incorporates modern vector and matrix instruction extensions including AVX-512 and Intel AMX (amx_tile and amx_int8), alongside hardware cryptographic acceleration via VAES and SHA-NI.

Benchmark evaluations show that the instance exhibits average single-thread compute capabilities alongside lower aggregate multi-core and memory subsystem throughput. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU performance scored 1618.89, while multi-core performance reached 3315.66. Geekbench testing reflects a matching profile, recording a single-core score of 1713.0 and a multi-core score of 3813.0. Memory bandwidth benchmarks recorded 28.42 GB/sec for large uncached block reads and 21.13 GB/sec for writes. The machine achieves 6.68 GB/sec in static web serving throughput and handles 4.42 million Redis SET operations per second.

The c3-standard-4 does not include local disk storage or onboard GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage for persistence. Because of its core count constraints, the instance exhibits lower overall throughput in heavy multi-threaded tasks such as parallel decompression or compute-heavy compiling. However, its dedicated CPU allocation, modern instruction set support, and balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio provide steady baseline execution for web serving, microservices, lightweight application backends, and standard continuous integration jobs.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3-standard-4 is a general-purpose compute instance equipped with 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores, powered by an Intel Xeon 8481C processor clocked at 2.7 GHz with 16 GB of memory. It features advanced x86_64 instruction extensions including AVX-512, AMX, and cryptographic acceleration. The instance does not bundle local disk storage or hardware accelerators, depending on remote storage volumes for persistent data. In benchmark evaluations, the c3-standard-4 displays solid single-core metrics, registering a Geekbench single-core score of 1713.0 and a stress-ng score of 1618.89, while multi-threaded and memory bandwidth metrics reflect its compact core footprint. With a 6.68 GB/sec static web serving capacity and 4.42 million Redis SET operations per second, this server type delivers a balanced configuration for web serving, standard business logic, microservices, and general-purpose production workloads.
